artists.biography: Gin Blossoms are an American pop rock band formed in 1987 in Tempe, Arizona. They broke out with the song "Hey Jealousy" from their successful major label debut, New Miserable Experience (1992), but this achievement was coupled with the firing and eventual suicide of the song's author and band co-founder Doug Hopkins, prompting the title of their follow-up album, Congratulations I'm Sorry (1996). After a series of charting singles, the band broke up in 1997. After they reunited in 2002 they released a fourth album, Major Lodge Victory, in 2006, and their fifth, No Chocolate Cake, in 2010.

They broke out with the song "Hey Jealousy" from their successful major label debut, New Miserable Experience (1992), but this achievement was coupled with the firing and eventual suicide of the song's author and band co-founder Doug Hopkins, prompting the title of their follow-up album, Congratulations I'm Sorry (1996). After a series of charting singles, the band broke up in 1997. After they reunited in 2002 they released a fourth album, Major Lodge Victory, in 2006, and their fifth, No Chocolate Cake, in 2010.

perplexity.description:
Released on August 4, 1992, New Miserable Experience is the second studio album by American rock band Gin Blossoms and their first full-length release for A&M Records. The album is a defining example of early 1990s alternative rock and power pop, blending jangly guitar melodies, catchy hooks, and introspective lyrics. Its sound is rooted in the band’s Arizona origins, combining accessible pop sensibilities with a slightly melancholic undercurrent, characteristic of the era’s guitar-driven rock.

New Miserable Experience marked a turning point in the Gin Blossoms’ career, establishing them as mainstream rock figures. Although the album initially received modest attention and lukewarm reviews, its fortunes changed with the release of singles like “Hey Jealousy” and “Found Out About You,” which became radio staples and propelled the album to multi-platinum status. The record also features other notable tracks such as “Mrs. Rita,” “Allison Road,” and “Until I Fall Away,” showcasing the band’s knack for melodic songwriting. Despite a rocky start and personal turmoil within the band—most notably the departure of guitarist Doug Hopkins during recording—the album endures as a quintessential release in the band’s discography and a touchstone of 1990s pop-rock.
